question: You issue stateless JWT access tokens valid for 24 hours. Security asks: when an admin disables an account, how is the user logged out immediately?
context: Tokens are verified by signature only, with no lookup. Several services accept the same token. "Immediately" means within seconds, not hours.

options.label: Nothing to change — the signature is still valid, so the token is still valid
options.why: That is exactly the problem being reported. A stateless token remains acceptable until it expires; a disabled account can keep working for the rest of the day.

options.label: Short-lived access tokens plus a refresh token checked against server state
options.why: Access tokens live minutes, so a disabled account stops working almost at once; the refresh step is the checkpoint where revocation is enforced. This keeps the common path stateless without pretending revocation is free.

options.label: Rotate the signing key so every token becomes invalid
options.why: It does log the user out — along with every other user, on every service. A blunt instrument for a per-account action, and it breaks key rotation hygiene.

options.label: Switch entirely to server-side sessions
options.why: Revocation becomes trivial, and this is a legitimate design — but it is a bigger change than the problem requires and gives up the stateless verification other services rely on. Consider it if you find yourself checking state on every request anyway.
